name: Indomethacin Embryofetopathy

criteria.description: Confirmed prenatal exposure to indomethacin during the first or second trimester
Premature closure or constriction of the fetal ductus arteriosus detected by prenatal ultrasound
Presence of skeletal abnormalities including limb contractures and hypoplasia
Evidence of pulmonary hypoplasia on imaging or clinical examination
Signs of neonatal renal impairment or oligohydramnios during pregnancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Confirmed prenatal indomethacin exposure plus at least two major criteria including ductus arteriosus closure and skeletal malformations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by prenatal history and imaging findings.

laboratory: Oligohydramnios detected by amniotic fluid index measurement
Neonatal renal function tests showing impaired glomerular filtration
Transient thrombocytopenia on complete blood count
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing premature ductus arteriosus closure
Chest X-ray or fetal MRI demonstrating pulmonary hypoplasia
Skeletal survey revealing limb contractures and rib hypoplasia
genetic: No known genetic mutations; condition is teratogenic due to drug exposure
other: History of maternal indomethacin use during pregnancy
Neonatal clinical examination showing arthrogryposis and respiratory distress

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic etiology with variable inheritance patterns
Absence of ductus arteriosus closure abnormalities
Presence of maternal rubella infection during pregnancy

redFlags: History of maternal indomethacin use during pregnancy
Prenatal ultrasound showing ductus arteriosus constriction or closure
Neonatal respiratory distress with limb contractures
references: Brent RL. Teratogen update: Indomethacin. Teratology. 1995;51(5):374-382.
Miller RK. Drug use in pregnancy. N Engl J Med. 1998;338(16):1128-1137.
